messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Morgan <alice.morgan@clearshore.com>, security@clearshore.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transient auth surge — IR procedures, artifact handoff, and postmortem timeline

Alice / Clearshore team —

Quick heads-up from Redwood: overnight we observed a transient surge of anomalous authentication requests affecting a small subset of Clearshore's tenant activity (no authorized data exfil observed). We wanted to notify you immediately, outline our containment steps, and provide the artifacts we can share while we complete the post-incident review.

What we did (initial containment):
- Identified spike at 2028-04-26T01:42:15Z affecting token exchange endpoints behind tenant-403.
- Auto-throttled suspicious IP ranges and rotated a short-lived service token used by a diagnostic job.
- Kicked off telemetry collection and snapshot of KV caches.

What we are sharing now: redacted telemetry extracts and a copy of the current IR procedures for partner-facing incidents. See attachments: redacted-telemetry-20280426.csv, irp_v2.pdf. Full evidence bundle is staged (evidence_bundle_20280426.zip) for secure transfer per your preference.

Next steps we propose:
1) Immediate: confirm which evidence transfer mechanism you prefer (secure SFTP vs. pre-signed S3 URL).
2) By EOD (our timezone): deliver a sanitized evidence bundle and a short containment timeline.
3) Within 72 hrs: provide a postmortem draft and proposed remediation items.

If you want an immediate bridge, we can open a 30-minute call with L3 and our security lead.

Apologies for the disruption — we prioritize transparency here. Please advise how you want the artifacts delivered and any legal/forensic redaction constraints.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (555) 312-4021

Subject: Postmortem + timeline (draft) — transient auth surge (Clearshore tenant)

Alice / Clearshore —

Thank you again for the bridge yesterday. Attached is a short draft postmortem and an initial list of remediation items. High-level summary:

- Root cause (interim): a misconfigured internal diagnostic job used a long-lived token which, under increased rotation latency, allowed repeated token exchange attempts originating from a misrouted test cluster.
- Impact: transient auth attempts against Clearshore tenant; no verified credential compromise and no confirmed data exfiltration.
- Containment: throttled IP ranges (see Marissa's note), rotated the diagnostic token, and implemented a temporary reject rule for token exchange endpoints for test clusters.

Remediation workstreams (ETA):
1) Token lifecycle enforcement — change scheduled for 2028-05-03 (infra).
2) Improved telemetry alerting to detect exchange-rate anomalies — 2028-05-10 (SRE).
3) Tenant-level hardening guide for customers (draft attached) — 2028-05-17 (Customer Security).

We intend to produce a final postmortem after a full log reconciliation (expected within 72 hours). For compliance: we will provide a redaction attestation document and a signed chain-of-custody for the evidence transfer.

If you need a formal SOC2/ISO annotation for this event, loop in your compliance contact; we will prepare an excerpt.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
